references.text: Earlier in the same chapter, God repeats that their dead bodies will fall in the wilderness, especially those who were counted from twenty years old and upward and who grumbled against the Lord.
The fulfillment of judgment: none from the first census survived except Caleb and Joshua, because the Lord had said they would die in the wilderness.
Moses recounts God's judgment that none of that evil generation would see the good land which God had promised.
Describes how the entire generation of fighting men died out in the wilderness until they were wiped out from the camp, as the Lord had sworn.
The psalm reminds us how God raised His hand against them and swore to let them fall in the wilderness.
Ezekiel refers to how God swore in the wilderness that He would not bring them into the land because of their disobedience.
Hebrews asks whom God was angry with for forty years—was it not those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?
